concept.title: Torsion local-global compatibility at p = ℓ for GL_n over CM fields
concept.concept_description: Conjecture that a torsion Hecke eigenclass in the cohomology of the arithmetic manifold attached to GL_n over a CM number field F with coefficients in Z/ℓ^m gives rise to a continuous semisimple Galois representation r : G_F → GL_n(Z_ℓ) which is de Rham at places v|ℓ, with Hodge–Tate weights determined by the infinitesimal character of the automorphic representation at infinity, and whose associated filtered φ‑module via Fontaine's functor corresponds under the p‑adic local Langlands correspondence to the automorphic component π_v.
concept.mathematical_framing: Conjecture that a torsion Hecke eigenclass in the cohomology of the arithmetic manifold attached to GL_n over a CM number field F with coefficients in Z/ℓ^m gives rise to a continuous semisimple Galois representation r : G_F → GL_n(Z_ℓ) which is de Rham at places v|ℓ, with Hodge–Tate weights determined by the infinitesimal character of the automorphic representation at infinity, and whose associated filtered φ‑module via Fontaine's functor corresponds under the p‑adic local Langlands correspondence to the automorphic component π_v.
concept.lean_guess: Extend Scholze's construction of automorphic determinants to Z_ℓ-coefficients, use the comparison isomorphism between étale and de Rham cohomology (via p-adic Hodge theory) to obtain de Rham Galois representations, then apply the p-adic local Langlands correspondence for GL_n over local fields to match the local Langlands parameter at places dividing ℓ with the automorphic data.

concept.title: Manifold-Constrained Kruskal Rank Bounds on Dichotomy Counts
concept.concept_description: For a d-dimensional submanifold E of ℝ^M and a smooth injective map Φ:E→ℝ^{M'}, any N-point set F⊂E in general position satisfies Kruskal rank s ≤ d+1. This implies the Φ-separable dichotomy count C_F(N) is bounded by Cover's counting function C(N,d+M'+1), generalizing high-dimensional bounds to low-dimensional data structures.
concept.mathematical_framing: For a d-dimensional submanifold E of ℝ^M and a smooth injective map Φ:E→ℝ^{M'}, any N-point set F⊂E in general position satisfies Kruskal rank s ≤ d+1. This implies the Φ-separable dichotomy count C_F(N) is bounded by Cover's counting function C(N,d+M'+1), generalizing high-dimensional bounds to low-dimensional data structures.
concept.lean_guess: 1) Characterize smooth injective maps on submanifolds via local charts. 2) Bound the Kruskal rank using dimension arguments: each additional point can increase rank by at most 1 until reaching d+1. 3) Relate this rank constraint to dichotomy counts via Cover's lemma. 4) Verify tightness with synthetic low-dimensional examples.

concept.title: Andrew's theorem is asymptotically tight for maximal vertex counts of lattice polytopes
concept.concept_description: For each dimension d ≥ 1, the upper bound on the number of vertices of a d-dimensional lattice polytope in terms of its volume given by Andrew's theorem is asymptotically optimal. Specifically, there exists a sequence of lattice polytopes with volumes V_n → ∞ such that the number of vertices m_n satisfies lim sup (m_n / V_n^{d/(d-1)}) = c_d, where c_d is the constant from Andrew's theorem.
concept.mathematical_framing: For each dimension d ≥ 1, the upper bound on the number of vertices of a d-dimensional lattice polytope in terms of its volume given by Andrew's theorem is asymptotically optimal. Specifically, there exists a sequence of lattice polytopes with volumes V_n → ∞ such that the number of vertices m_n satisfies lim sup (m_n / V_n^{d/(d-1)}) = c_d, where c_d is the constant from Andrew's theorem.
concept.lean_guess: Construct explicit families of scaled and sheared lattice polytopes (e.g., hypercubes with strategically perturbed facets) whose vertex counts approach the asymptotic bound. Utilize the paper's key technique of volume-preserving transformations to show that the reverse isoperimetric inequality allows arbitrarily high vertex counts while maintaining volume control.

concept.concept_description: Borges' Library of Babel contains every possible 410-page book — approximately 25^{1312000} volumes. The library is finite but vast beyond comprehension. Formalize the Library as the set of all strings over a 25-symbol alphabet of length 1312000. Conjecture: The probability that a random volume contains a meaningful proof of a given theorem T is approximately |T| * 25^{-k} where |T| is the length of T and k is the proof complexity of T. Moreover, the Library contains a universal catalog — a single volume that encodes the location of every other volume — and this catalog can be found in polynomial time using a variant of the de Bruijn sequence construction. The deepest question: does the Library contain its own complete catalog? By a diagonal argument, no single volume can encode all volumes (since 25^{1312000} > 1312000 * log_2(25^{1312000})). But a DISTRIBUTED catalog spanning N volumes can encode the entire Library if N > 25^{1312000} / (1312000 * log_2(25)). Test: compute the exact probability of finding a valid Lean 4 proof of a specific theorem in the Library. Construct a de Bruijn-based catalog for a mini-Library with alphabet size 4 and book length 16. Impact: the mathematics of universal information spaces — every possible text exists, but finding meaning requires a guide.
